profileRouting.evidence: Two Safari profiles connected to a newly started server within 25 s without anyone opening the popup (7.6 s and 3.5 s in two runs). In each profile, tabs_create opened a marked tab, and tabs_create with newWindow opened a window of its own and returned that window's tab. All four tabs reached the right page by handle, followed select_tab for untargeted calls, and answered read_page and snapshot.

profileReconnect.evidence: Disabling the extension in the second profile disconnected it while the default profile stayed connected and drivable; a call naming the absent profile was refused with profile_not_connected. Re-enabling it reconnected the profile under the same handle, and it listed its tabs again.

permissions.evidence: The first call on an undecided site (rfc-editor.org) failed in 9 ms with permission_required and said how to allow the site from the toolbar button. After the user allowed the site there, the same call worked and tabs_context described the tab. tabs_create on a site the user had already allowed (iana.org) returned access granted with the page title, and the next call on that tab worked. Safari 27.2 shows no permission dialog.

privateByDefault.evidence: Across both profiles (47 tabs), every tab not known to be granted was listed without url or title (45 withheld, none leaking), each with an accessHint saying why.
